alternatives.name: Attached LTE modem + flat antenna — ENGINEERING OPTION / untested
alternatives.note: No genuinely smaller-footprint complete board verified: HAT 65 × 30.5 mm is shorter but wider than Pico 73.5 × 24 mm, not smaller overall. Connectors, wiring and height need extra enclosure space; not verified to fit the supplied display case. HAT SKU17693: $32.99, 3.3V UART logic but 5V power. Never power the modem from the display 3.3V rail. Exact non-touch V2 schematic/pinout and power ratings remain unresolved; no ready-attach or numbered pin-to-pin wiring is approved. Do not parallel chargers or assume a shared battery is safe. Taoglas FXP40.07.0085A: $1.82, 42.6 × 12.1 mm, 85 mm coax, MHF I / U.FL-compatible, not SMA or MHF4. Exact HAT RF connector matching is unconfirmed; an adapter may add cost/height. Retailer lead time 2–3 weeks or less; nonreturnable (NCNR), not verified in-hand stock. LTE bands 12/13 are covered, but low-band antenna efficiency is only 12% in free space / 17% on 2 mm ABS. Compactness trades away RF performance; test indoor reception and hand loading. Mount on plastic, separated from battery foil/display metal; verify antenna and host regulatory integration before deployment. Known $34.81 is modem board + antenna only. Required power/boost, wiring, mounting/enclosure, SIM/service and possible RF adapter are unpriced; shipping and tax unknown. Complete cellular cost and all-parts arrival remain unknown. Firmware is not implemented: add audio compression/decoding and buffering, modem AT/control and UART flow control, SIM/APN/LTE-M registration, data transport, authenticated TLS to the Hermes bridge, reconnect/backoff and sustained bidirectional audio tests. Existing Wi-Fi firmware is not a modem client. Confirm physical 1.8V-capable SIM, carrier/IMEI eligibility and local attach; prefer LTE-M, not NB-IoT, for interactive audio. Bench-test with independently correct host/HAT power and verified common logic ground; resolve UART boot-log conflicts and prevent backfeeding. Size and measure peak-current power delivery before any shared-battery design. No prototype or hardware qualification is claimed.
